texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, using short snake_case codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; never raise bare ValueError.
texts.at-0003: Exclude bool when validating integer inputs When validating an int parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) because True/False pass isinstance(x, int) in Python.
texts.at-0004: Use money helpers for Decimal conversion and rounding Convert amounts with `ledgerly.money.to_money` and round results with `ledgerly.money.round_money` (ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent) instead of using floats or `round()`.
texts.at-0005: Raise BillingError with a snake_case code Signal invalid input by raising `ledgerly.errors.BillingError(code, detail)` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_tax_rate`, not ValueError.

review_comments: [team convention] Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end and always has exactly two decimal places. Never convert amounts to float.
